title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily brief (Fri, 16 Oct 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. Ordering is inferred from cross-category relevance and author-reported evaluation evidence; independent popularity/citation momentum could not be corroborated for these very recent papers. Results are preprint claims.

sections.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
sections.abstract: The paper presents MLExpert, a 35B mixture-of-experts agent trained for long-horizon ML engineering, and reports that its average medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite rises from 37.9% for its base model to 72.7% after training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Hierarchical Agentic SFT and Windowed Interaction RL, and report generalization to NatureBench Lite and optimization tasks beyond MLE-Bench Lite.
sections.unique_caveat: The primary result is on a 22-task MLE-Bench Lite subset, so it does not establish broad autonomous-research capability.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Triple-listed across core AI categories and reports a concrete benchmark result; relevance signal, not readership evidence.

sections.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
sections.abstract: LEASH routes work from a weaker agent to a stronger one using latent uncertainty and continues monitoring after handoff; on OSWorld, the authors report 73.66% success at $0.4117 per task for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, with a 19.2% inference-cost reduction versus always-on Claude Opus 5.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine initial routing, step-level escalation, and shadow oversight using a reference-based latent uncertainty estimate.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say evaluation is limited to computer use; the uncertainty score predicts weak-agent failure risk rather than expected escalation benefit, and the oversight intervention is not causally isolated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports controlled OSWorld results across four model backbones with cost/success comparisons.

sections.title: TIPS: A Tiny Inference-time Policy for Scaling in Diffusion Language Models
sections.abstract: TIPS is an approximately 600K-parameter controller that learns when to reveal or remask tokens in a frozen masked-diffusion language model, reporting 58.46% and 57.97% micro-averaged accuracy on GSM8K and MATH-500 at 32 decoder evaluations for two variants.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train a lightweight visibility controller with supervised warmup and terminal-reward reinforcement learning while leaving the backbone unchanged.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline evaluation uses one backbone (LLaDA-8B-Instruct) and two math benchmarks, so generality to other models and task types remains open.

sections.title: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty
sections.abstract: CATCH adversarially trains models toward honest and away from dishonest answers; the authors report transfer across distinct honesty benchmarks from hundreds of self-reporting targets, with utility retention on two model architectures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that CATCH improves honesty over prompting and supervised fine-tuning, and matches activation steering while better preserving utility.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is from two model architectures and selected honesty settings; transfer to other models and real-world behavior is not established.

sections.title: CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering
sections.abstract: CARA guides knowledge-graph retrieval using tests of whether evidence improves or is necessary for answering, and reports better retrieval and answer quality with fewer nodes and retrieval operations across three STaRK datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine consequentiality, essentiality, path consistency, and reciprocal-rank fusion in a training-free retrieval agent.
sections.unique_caveat: The study targets text-rich knowledge-graph retrieval; its question-answering evaluation augments STaRK with ground-truth answers, so the results do not establish gains for general-purpose RAG.

sections.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
sections.abstract: Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator as a single-pass feed-forward system for 4D geometry and motion from monocular video, reporting state-of-the-art or competitive results on point tracking, video depth, and camera-pose estimation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use on-demand spatial and continuous-time queries plus a frozen video-depth LoRA prior to decode 4D attributes from clean video latents.
sections.unique_caveat: The work is scoped to monocular-video perception and the listed geometry tasks; the abstract does not provide enough detail to assess performance across broader video domains.

sections.title: AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations
sections.abstract: AgentPerturb evaluates agents under controlled interaction changes on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon, finding performance degradation and environment-dependent vulnerabilities, with corrupted information often propagated without verification.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a two-dimensional framework for perturbation targets and types and use trajectory-level analysis to motivate robustness-oriented training.
sections.unique_caveat: Findings are limited to the two tested environments; the authors note that dominant vulnerabilities vary by task environment.

sections.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: LIBERO-PeRM introduces five simulated task suites (312 tasks) for measuring whether robot policies follow, learn, generalize, and resolve conflicts among user preferences; its experiments find current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that supervised fine-tuning makes preferences learnable and that mixed training can improve preference performance while retaining no-preference behavior better than sequential adaptation.
sections.unique_caveat: Preferences are language-expressible, instantiated in LIBERO simulation, and constrained not to change task goals; this does not yet demonstrate personalization in physical homes.
